title: Ukraine: Russian attacks leave tens of thousands without power
summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Russia struck energy infrastructure in at least four regions overnight. Meanwhile, a Melania Trump-brokered ceasefire for the Kherson region is set to end on Sunday evening.…
byline: Karl Sexton, Richard Connor, Darko Janjevic

image.caption: Russian drones were flying over Kyiv on SundayImage: Vladyslav Musiienko/AFP

blocks.text: Melania Trump-brokered ceasefire for Kherson set to expire

blocks.caption: Some 750 civilians were due to be evacuated from Oleshky during the truce, Melania Trump had saidImage: Evgeniy Maloletka/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: A ceasefire limited to the Kherson region in eastern Ukraine that was brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump was set to expire on Sunday evening, after neither Russia nor Ukraine announced an extension.
The rare truce, which began on Tuesday, is the longest since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
The ceasefire allowed for a humanitarian mission to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky.

While neither side reported violations of the ceasefire, Russian strikes continued overnight, with fresh power outages reported across Ukraine on Sunday, its energy ministry and president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.
Ukrainian strikes on the Russian-occupied region of Luhansk killed at least four people since Sunday evening, Russian-backed local authorities said.
